note: Catalog profiles: which document types count as core for a kind of project. `default` is tier.core in CATALOG-RULES.json; every other profile is a delta of `add` and `remove`, so a profile is small, reviewable, and cannot silently redefine the default set. A removal must name a default core type; an addition must be an id the catalog knows, carry a reason, and state the phases it is off in (its severity_by_phase), because "core for this kind of project" still does not mean "required at idea". Selecting a profile is a declaration (autodoc.toml `profile`), never an inference. MEMBERSHIP AWAITS OWNER REVIEW: these are a defensible starting point, not a survey.

profiles.name: Default
profiles.why: The set that survives every project shape: the idea and build documents plus the ones already gated by a detected fact.

profiles.name: Startup
profiles.why: Small team, changing direction: a written roadmap earns its place, while lifecycle promises made before product-market fit are theatre.

add.why: Direction changes often and out loud; a written roadmap keeps the team pointing the same way.

remove.why: A deprecation promise is about consumers you do not have yet; it becomes real once there are users.

profiles.name: Open-source library
profiles.why: Consumers you will never meet, contributing strangers, and redistribution: the social documents are load-bearing.

add.why: A public community needs a stated standard of behaviour and a way to report a breach.
A published package needs a disclosure route for vulnerabilities, as SECURITY.md.
Dependency policy is the maintainer's stated answer to supply-chain questions.

remove.why: A library is not operated; there is no on-call rotation for a package.

profiles.name: Internal service
profiles.why: Operated by the same organisation that owns it: operations documents are core, and distribution documents are not.

add.why: Someone is on call; the rotation and its expectations must be written.
An internal service still needs a stated reliability target and the error budget it implies.
Incidents happen to internal services too, and the response path should not be improvised.

remove.why: An internal service is not redistributed, so there are no external licence terms to state.

profiles.name: Regulated
profiles.why: Personal data, auditors, and evidence: claims must be traceable to records that outlive the people who wrote them.

add.why: Processing personal data requires a record of what is processed, why, and with whom it is shared.
Retention must be decided before data accumulates, not after someone asks.
Controls are only credible when they are catalogued and mapped to evidence.
Access reviews are the evidence auditors ask for first; the record is the deliverable.
